mainTopic: Redeeming fields and walled-city houses: counting the redemption year, and whether the refund counts as ריבית
overview: The amud opens by settling two ברייתות about redeeming a field. One allows borrowing to redeem it and redeeming it in parts, and the other forbids both. They follow the רבנן and רבי שמעון. A new משנה then teaches about a house sold in a walled city. The seller may buy it back right away and for twelve months, counted from the first sale. The rights pass to heirs, and the year includes a leap month (רבי says a full solar year). After the year, the house is the buyer's forever, even if he received it as a gift. The גמרא notes that the משנה does not follow רבי, who learns from ימים that the seller must wait two days. It then works out which words in the פסוקים each side uses to teach that the year runs from the sale date, ends at the exact hour of the sale, and includes the leap month. Finally, the משנה calls the refund 'like interest,' while a ברייתא calls it real interest that the Torah permitted. רבי יוחנן says this depends on whether צד אחד ברבית is forbidden (the רבנן) or permitted (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Two ברייתות clash about borrowing to redeem a field
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows borrowing money to redeem and allows redeeming in parts. Another ברייתא forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a person may borrow money and redeem his field, and he may redeem it in parts. Another ברייתא teaches: he may not borrow and redeem, and he may not redeem in parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two ברייתות side by side that say the exact opposite about redeeming a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא allows two things: borrowing to redeem, and redeeming bit by bit. The second ברייתא forbids both. Two teachings cannot both be right unless something explains the gap, so the גמרא needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrows money and uses it to redeem
Redeems in halves, meaning paying for part of the field at a time
The other one (here, the other ברייתא)

phrases.english: It is taught in one baraita:
One may borrow and redeem,
and one may redeem in halves;
and it is taught in another baraita:
One may not borrow and redeem,
and one may not redeem in halves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a contradiction between two ברייתות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the ברייתות on redeeming a field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא permits borrowing and partial redemption, and the other forbids both, so they directly contradict each other.

steps.title: The ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: There is no real clash. One ברייתא follows the רבנן and the other follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows the רבנן, and that ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by saying each ברייתא reflects a different תנא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict ברייתא, which forbids borrowing and partial redemption, follows the רבנן. The lenient ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who is lenient about redeeming a field (here, from הקדש). Since they come from different opinions, they no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real problem
The Sages (the majority opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not match the two words הָא by their order in the sentence. The ruling that forbids borrowing is the רבנן's view, and the ruling that allows it is רבי שמעון's lenient view.
steps.whatToRemember: When two ברייתות clash, the גמרא often explains that each follows a different תנא.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is the Rabbis, and that one is Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: The ruling that forbids borrowing goes with the Rabbis; the one that allows it goes with רבי שמעון, who is more lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבָּנַן וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to state a single rule that everyone agrees on, so they appeared to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict ברייתא follows the רבנן and the lenient one follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: משנה: redeeming a house in a walled city
steps.stepSummary: The seller may redeem the house right away and throughout the first twelve months. This looks like ריבית, but it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who sells a house in a walled city may redeem it immediately, and he may redeem it during the whole twelve months. This looks like a kind of interest, but it is not interest.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the seller of a house in a walled city has a twelve-month window to buy it back, starting right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller does not have to wait at all. He can redeem the house immediately and at any point within twelve months. If he redeems it, the buyer lived in the house for free while the seller held his money, which looks like ריבית. It is not, because the house truly belonged to the buyer during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Houses in cities that are surrounded by a wall
May redeem immediately, with no waiting period
Looks like a form of interest

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic twelve-month window that the rest of the משנה builds on.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sells a house among the houses of walled cities,
may redeem it immediately,
and may redeem it during all twelve months;
this is like a form of interest,
but it is not interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller may redeem the house from right away through twelve months, and this is not ריבית.

steps.title: The right to redeem passes to heirs
steps.stepSummary: If the seller dies, his son may redeem. If the buyer dies, the seller may redeem from the buyer's son.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller died, his son may redeem the house. If the buyer died, the seller may redeem it from the buyer's son.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that death on either side does not cancel the right to redeem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right to redeem is not personal to the seller, so it passes to his son. In the same way, the buyer's heirs take over the house still subject to that right.

keyTerms.meaning: The seller
The buyer
From the possession of his son

phrases.english: If the seller died, his son may redeem;
if the buyer died, he may redeem it from the possession of his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the right to redeem to cases where the seller or buyer has died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The right to redeem passes to the seller's heir and can be used against the buyer's heir.

steps.title: The year counts from the original sale
steps.stepSummary: The twelve months are counted from the time the owner sold the house, based on the words עד מלאת לו שנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The year is counted only from the time he sold it, as it says: 'until a full year passes for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה fixes the starting point of the twelve months and gives a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לו ('for him') ties the year to the original seller. So even if the house is resold to someone else, the clock is not restarted. It keeps running from the first sale.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not count
Until a year is completed for him (ויקרא 25:30)

phrases.english: One does not count the year
except from the time that he sold it,
phrases.notes: He means the first sale by the original owner, even if the buyer later sold it again.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Until the passing of a full year for him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹנִין שָׁנָה אֶלָּא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁמָּכַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines when the twelve-month window from step 3 begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption year runs from the original sale.

steps.title: The word 'full' includes a leap month
steps.stepSummary: The word תמימה teaches that an added leap month is counted as part of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Torah says 'full,' it comes to include the leap month.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reads the word תמימה to teach that in a leap year, the year lasts thirteen months.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this word, one might count exactly twelve months even in a leap year. The word 'full' means the whole calendar year, including the extra month.

keyTerms.meaning: Full, complete (said about the year in the פסוק)
The extra month added in a leap year
To include

phrases.english: When it says 'full,'
phrases.notes: This is from the same פסוק, ויקרא 25:30: 'a full year.'

phrases.english: it is to include the intercalated month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further defines the length of the year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a leap year, the leap month is part of the redemption year.

steps.title: רבי: a year plus its added days
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads 'full' as giving the seller a solar year, meaning the lunar year plus the extra days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: it is to give him a year and its addition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי offers a different reading of the word תמימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, as רש״י explains, 'full' means a complete solar year rather than a lunar year, whether or not the year has a leap month. Later the גמרא says that רבי also counts the leap month. So the seller gets the extra days added onto the lunar year.

keyTerms.meaning: A year and its addition (the extra days of a solar year)

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
It is to give him a year and its addition.
phrases.notes: A full sun-based year of 365 days, not just the 354 days of a moon-based year.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לִיתֵּן לוֹ שָׁנָה וְעִיבּוּרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative reading of the word תמימה from step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption year is a full solar year.

steps.title: After twelve months the house is the buyer's forever
steps.stepSummary: If the house is not redeemed by the end of twelve months, it belongs to the buyer permanently. This applies to a gift as well, based on לצמיתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the day ending the twelve months arrived and the house was not redeemed, it became permanently his. This is true both for a buyer and for someone who received it as a gift, as it says: 'in perpetuity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by saying what happens when the twelve months pass, and it applies the rule to a gift too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the window closes, the house becomes חלוטה, fully and permanently owned. It does not even return in יובל. The word לצמיתות shows that this applies not only to a buyer but also to someone who received the house as a gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanently and fully owned
A gift
In perpetuity, forever (ויקרא 25:30)

steps.whatToRemember: A house in a walled city: it can be redeemed for twelve months from the first sale, and after that it is the buyer's forever, whether he bought it or received it as a gift.

phrases.english: If the day of the twelve months arrived
and it was not redeemed,
it has become his permanently.
Both the one who buys
and the one to whom it is given as a gift,
as it is stated: 'In perpetuity.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ יוֹם שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא נִגְאֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States what happens when the redemption window from step 3 ends, and widens the rule to include gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unredeemed house becomes the buyer's or the gift recipient's permanently after twelve months.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי's two-day rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה (redeem immediately) disagrees with רבי, who learns from ימים that the seller cannot redeem for the first two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה is not like רבי. A ברייתא teaches that רבי says: the word 'days' means no fewer than two days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that our משנה, which lets the seller buy back the house right away, goes against רבי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ימים תהיה גאלתו', meaning 'for days he shall have redemption.' רבי reads the plural ימים as at least two days, so the seller must wait two days before redeeming. The משנה follows the רבנן, who allow redemption immediately.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Not in line with the opinion of...
'Days' means at least two days

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying the seller has only two days to redeem. He means the seller cannot redeem until two days have passed.

phrases.english: Gemara: Our mishna is not like Rabbi,
as it is taught: Rabbi says:
"Days" means no fewer than two days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the seller may redeem only after at least two days. The משנה, which allows redeeming right away, does not follow him.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from the word 'days'?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן do not learn a two-day wait, what do they do with ימים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word 'days'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the word ימים, since they do not use it for the two-day rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word in the פסוק must teach something. If the רבנן allow redemption right away, the word ימים needs another use.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it, meaning what do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this word "days"
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the other side how they use the word רבי used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's use of the word ימים.

steps.title: The רבנן: the year is counted day to day
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ימים to teach that the year is counted from the date of sale to the same date the next year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it to teach 'from day to day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn from ימים that the year runs from the day of the sale to the same day a year later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, one might think the year ends at ראש השנה. ימים teaches that we count full days from the actual sale date.

keyTerms.meaning: From day to day, from the date of sale to the same date next year
He needs it (to teach something else)

phrases.english: They need it for "from day to day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ימים teaches that the year is counted from the date of sale.

steps.title: Where does רבי learn 'day to day'?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי used ימים for the two-day rule, where does he learn day-to-day counting?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, where does he learn 'from day to day'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי and asks how he knows the year is counted from the sale date, since he already used ימים for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the rule of day-to-day counting. The question is only which words of the פסוק teach it according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi, from where does he learn "from day to day"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same kind of question back on רבי.

steps.title: רבי learns it from 'the year of its sale'
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns day-to-day counting from the words עד תום שנת ממכרו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'until the completion of the year of its sale.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי learns day-to-day counting from the phrase 'until the end of the year of its sale.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A year 'of its sale' starts from the sale itself, so it ends on the same date a year later. This frees ימים for רבי's two-day rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
Until the completion of the year of its sale

phrases.english: He derives it
from "until the completion of the year of its sale."

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״עַד תּוֹם שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי learns day-to-day counting from עד תום שנת ממכרו.

steps.title: The רבנן: it is the seller's own year, not the calendar year
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use שנת ממכרו to teach that the year is personal to this sale and is not the world's calendar year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They need that phrase to teach that it is the year of his own sale, not a year of the world's count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with 'the year of its sale' and answers that they use it to teach that the year belongs to this sale, not to the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use this phrase only to rule out counting by the calendar year. For the exact way of counting the days, they still rely on ימים, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: The world's count, the regular calendar year
His own, meaning the year of this particular sale

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? They need that phrase
for the year of his own sale,
and not a year of the world's count.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets (שְׁנַת); the corrected wording is the one in square brackets (שָׁנָה). The meaning is the same.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן? הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ שְׁנַת מִמְכָּרוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the רבנן use the phrase רבי just used, and answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שנת ממכרו excludes the calendar year.

steps.title: The רבנן: 'days' teaches counting to the exact hour
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן add that ימים teaches מעת לעת. The phrase about the year of sale alone would give only day-to-day counting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they need 'days' for counting from hour to hour. If we only had 'until the completion of the year of its sale,' I would have said day to day, yes, but hour to hour, no. So the Torah wrote 'days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that for the רבנן, ימים teaches that the year ends at the exact hour of the sale, not just on the right day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the רבנן's use of ימים grows from day-to-day counting to מעת לעת. The phrase about the year of sale would only show that we count by days, so the seller would lose the house as soon as that day began. ימים adds that he keeps the right to redeem until the exact hour of the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: From hour to hour, a full 24-hour-exact count
I would have thought
The Merciful One (the Torah) wrote

steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, the seller can still redeem on the last day until the exact hour when the sale happened a year earlier.

phrases.english: And they need "days" for "from hour to hour,"
for if it were from "until the completion of the year of its sale"
I would have said: from day to day, yes,
from hour to hour, no,
so the Merciful One wrote "days."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רבנן's answer by giving ימים a new job: exact-hour counting.

steps.title: Where does רבי learn counting to the exact hour?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי used ימים for the two-day rule, where does he learn מעת לעת?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי, where does he learn 'from hour to hour'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי gets the rule of counting to the exact hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי has already used ימים and שנת ממכרו for other rules, so he needs another word in the פסוק for מעת לעת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi, from where does he learn "from hour to hour"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question back to רבי.

steps.title: רבי learns it from 'full'
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns מעת לעת from the word תמימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'full.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי learns exact-hour counting from the word 'full' year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'full' year is only complete when every hour has passed. That gives רבי the מעת לעת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Full, complete (a full year)

phrases.english: He derives it from "full."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי learns מעת לעת from תמימה.

steps.title: The רבנן use 'full' for the leap month
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use תמימה to teach that an added leap month counts as part of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They need that word for its added month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the back-and-forth: the רבנן use תמימה to include the leap month in the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the earlier teaching that תמימה includes the leap month. So each side has a source for every rule. The two sides differ only in which word teaches which rule, and in רבי's two-day wait.

keyTerms.meaning: Its intercalation, the extra leap month added to the year

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: שנת ממכרו teaches that it is the seller's own year counted from the sale date (day to day), ימים teaches exact-hour counting (מעת לעת), and תמימה teaches that the leap month counts. The משנה, which allows redeeming right away, follows the רבנן. רבי's final set of sources comes in step 20.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? They need that for its added leap month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's use of תמימה and closes the cycle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use תמימה to include the leap month.

steps.title: רבי also needs תמימה for the leap month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי cannot use תמימה for מעת לעת, because he too needs it to teach that the leap month counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי also needs that word for including the leap month!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 17, which said רבי learns מעת לעת from תמימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the רבנן used תמימה to teach that a leap month counts in the year. רבי must agree with that rule too. So the word seems already taken, and he cannot also use it for מעת לעת.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra month added in a leap year
'Full' (the year), the word in the פסוק being discussed

phrases.english: And רבי too,
doesn't he need it for its leap month!
phrases.notes: 'It' is the word תמימה, which the רבנן used for the leap month in step 18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17 using the derivation brought in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי learns מעת לעת from תמימה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word cannot easily teach two rules, and רבי surely agrees the leap month counts, so תמימה is already used up.

steps.title: Both kinds of counting come from 'until the end of the year of its sale'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that רבי uses תמימה for the leap month. Both day-to-day and hour-to-hour counting come from 'עד תום שנת ממכרו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed so. Day-to-day and hour-to-hour are both learned from 'until the completion of the year of its sale.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and changes how רבי learns things. One phrase gives him both counting rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, תמימה goes to the leap month, just as it does for the רבנן. 'עד תום שנת ממכרו' gives both counting rules at once: the year runs from the date of the sale (מיום ליום), and it ends at the exact hour of the sale (מעת לעת). That leaves ימים free for his two-day rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting from the date of the sale, not by the calendar year
Counting from the exact hour of the sale
It is derived

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי: ימים teaches the two-day rule, תמימה teaches the leap month, and 'עד תום שנת ממכרו' teaches both day-to-day and hour-to-hour counting.

phrases.english: Indeed so;
day-to-day and hour-to-hour
are derived from 'until the completion of the year of its sale.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by giving רבי a new source for מעת לעת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the point and moves the derivation to a different phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי learns מעת לעת from תמימה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי uses תמימה for the leap month. Both day-to-day and hour-to-hour counting come from 'עד תום שנת ממכרו'.

steps.title: Is it 'like interest' or full interest?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה calls returning the full price 'like a form of רבית', but a ברייתא calls it full רבית that the Torah permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'This is like a form of interest.' But a ברייתא teaches: 'This is complete interest, only the Torah permitted it!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and sets it against a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller gets his house back, and the buyer gets back the full price he paid, even though he also lived in the house in the meantime. The משנה says this only looks like רבית. The ברייתא says it truly is רבית, and only the Torah's special permission allows it here.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that looks like interest but is not really interest
Real, complete interest
(The Torah) permitted it

phrases.english: 'This is like a form of interest,' etc.
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
This is complete interest,
but the Torah permitted it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זוֹ כְּמִין רִבִּית וְכוּ׳. וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the same arrangement real רבית, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה follows רבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is not difficult. This one is רבי יהודה, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן settles the contradiction by assigning each source to a different opinion. He will prove it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that this kind of sale is not real רבית at all, so for him it is only 'like' רבית. The רבנן hold that it is real רבית, so in the walled-city case it is allowed only because the Torah permitted it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty
This one follows one view, and that one follows another

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: It is not difficult;
this is רבי יהודה and that is the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak for one opinion and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא about selling a field for a debt
steps.stepSummary: A borrower 'sells' his field to the lender on a condition. If the seller eats the produce it is allowed; if the buyer eats it, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: One who was owed a מנה by his fellow, and the borrower made his field a sale to him. When the seller eats the produce, it is permitted. When the buyer eats the produce, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves רבי יוחנן's answer. This step gives the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sale is conditional, so if the loan is repaid the field goes back to the borrower. Then any produce the lender ate turns out to be payment for waiting on his money, which is real רבית. That is why the רבנן forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is owed money by (a creditor)
A sum of one hundred דינרים
He made his field a (conditional) sale to him
Eats (takes) the produce of the field

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'seller' is the borrower and the 'buyer' is the lender. Keep that straight or the whole case gets flipped.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One who was owed
a מנה by his fellow,
and he made his field a sale to him,
when the seller eats the produce, it is permitted;
if the buyer eats the produce, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה נוֹשֶׁה בַּחֲבֵירוֹ מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן treat this kind of arrangement as real רבית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a conditional sale of a field for a debt

steps.title: רבי יהודה permits even the buyer to eat the produce
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that even when the buyer eats the produce, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even when the buyer eats the produce, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי יהודה's view, which disagrees with the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה this arrangement is not real רבית. That fits the משנה's wording 'only like a form of רבית'.

keyTerms.meaning: The buyer (here, the lender)
Permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opinion that lets the משנה say 'כמין רבית', so it completes רבי יוחנן's answer.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַלּוֹקֵחַ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: Even when the buyer eats the produce, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the ברייתא's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conditional sale where the buyer eats the produce is permitted.

steps.title: The story of ביתוס בן זונין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a story: ביתוס בן זונין made such a sale on the instruction of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the buyer ate the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was an incident with ביתוס בן זונין, who made his field a sale on the instruction of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and the buyer was eating the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a real-life case to prove his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great sage, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, approved this arrangement. רבי יהודה says the buyer ate the produce in that case, so it must be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident
On the instruction of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבַיְתוֹס בֶּן זוֹנִין
phrases.english: רבי יהודה said: There was an incident with ביתוס בן זונין
who made his field a sale

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: on the instruction of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה,
and the buyer was eating the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's ruling in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That a buyer may eat the produce in a conditional sale
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of ביתוס בן זונין, decided by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה

steps.title: The רבנן reject the proof
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer that in that story the seller ate the produce, not the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You bring a proof from there? The seller was eating the produce, not the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן push away רבי יהודה's proof by telling the story differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller ate the produce, everyone agrees the arrangement is allowed. So the story proves nothing about the buyer eating, and the dispute stays as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof?
The seller (here, the borrower)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: a conditional sale is not real רבית, even when the buyer eats the produce, and the משנה's 'כמין רבית' follows him. רבנן: it is real רבית, and the ברייתא's 'רבית גמורה, but the Torah permitted it' follows them.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is there proof from there?

phrases.aramaic: מוֹכֵר אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת הָיָה, וְלֹא לוֹקֵחַ.
phrases.english: The seller was eating the produce, and not the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the story; רבי יהודה's ruling itself still stands as a view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The facts of the story were different: the seller ate the produce, which everyone permits.

steps.title: What is the core of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the argument between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what principle the two sides are really arguing about. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the ruling: the רבנן forbid the buyer (the lender) to eat the produce, and רבי יהודה permits it. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind the ruling, meaning which general rule each side holds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? The גמרא's way of asking for the real point of an argument.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבי יהודה and the רבנן from the last few steps, who argued about the lender eating the produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over the story of ביתוס בן זונין, the גמרא steps back to ask for the principle behind the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which underlying principle separates the רבנן, who forbid the buyer to eat the produce, from רבי יהודה, who permits it.

steps.title: They argue about interest that may or may not happen
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about צד אחד ברבית. The תנא קמא says it is forbidden, and רבי יהודה says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a deal that is interest only in one possible outcome. The first תנא holds that this kind of possible interest is forbidden, and רבי יהודה holds it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sides argue about צד אחד ברבית, a deal that might turn out to be interest and might not. The תנא קמא forbids it, and רבי יהודה allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower pays back the loan, the field returns to him, so the produce the lender ate was really extra payment for the loan, which is רבית. If the borrower does not pay back, the field belonged to the lender from the start, so he ate his own produce. Since the deal is רבית in only one of the two outcomes, the תנא קמא forbids it and רבי יהודה permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Interest on one side only: a deal that becomes interest only if things turn out a certain way.
Interest, which the Torah forbids a lender to take from a fellow Jew.
The first תנא, the opinion stated first without a name. Here it means the רבנן.
Forbidden / permitted.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument over the field 'sold' on condition comes down to one principle: the רבנן forbid צד אחד ברבית, and רבי יהודה permits it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה permits real interest. He permits only a deal where it is not yet clear whether it will ever be interest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns one specific case into a general rule, צד אחד ברבית, which applies to any deal that is interest only in one possible outcome.

phrases.english: Interest on one side is the difference between them,
phrases.notes: If the loan is repaid, the lender's eating was interest. If it isn't, the field was his all along, so there was no interest.

phrases.english: The first תנא holds:
interest on one side is forbidden,
and רבי יהודה holds:
interest on one side is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about צד אחד ברבית. The תנא קמא forbids it, and רבי יהודה permits it.
